name: Precise location
plain: Asks for the device's exact GPS position while the app is in use.
meaning: Reveals where a person is to within meters: home, work, routines, travel. Android's fine and iOS's precise grant are the most sensitive runtime permissions after background access.

android.prompt_ui: Android 12+: Precise or Approximate choice, then While using the app, Only this time, Don't allow
android.persistence: Until revoked or auto-reset; one-time grant ends when the app leaves view
android.revocation: Settings > Apps > Permissions > Location; Privacy dashboard
android.store_policy: Play: foreground location needs a prominent data-safety disclosure
android.note: Apps targeting 12 (API 31) must also declare COARSE; the user can downgrade to approximate.

ios.prompt_ui: Allow Once, Allow While Using App, Don't Allow; Precise Location toggle on the map card (iOS 14)
ios.persistence: Until revoked; Allow Once lapses after the app is backgrounded for a while
ios.store_policy: App Review 5.1.1 and 5.1.5: purpose string must be specific; location only for relevant features
ios.note: Precise is on by default; app can ask for temporary full accuracy with requestTemporaryFullAccuracyAuthorization.

data.update: one-shot or continuous, about 1 Hz when requested

limits.headline: Can see your exact GPS spot while you use the app, after you allow
limits.user_action: You tap Allow While Using the App with Precise on
can: Find your exact position within a few meters
Follow you as you move while the app is open
Show turn by turn directions or delivery tracking
Ask for full accuracy for a moment if you chose approximate (iPhone)
cannot: Follow you when the app is closed without Always allow
See your exact spot if you choose Approximate
Use the permission after you pick Don't Allow
Use your exact spot before you tap Allow
limits.reach_label: Exact spot, while the app is open
limits.differs: Android 12 and newer lets you downgrade to approximate in the prompt. iPhone has a Precise switch you can turn off.

story.what_it_is: An app learns exactly where you are, to within a few meters, while you use it.

marketing.name: Location Services
marketing.pitch: Apple lets you choose whether each app can see your exact location and when.

marketing.name: Precise location
marketing.pitch: Android lets you allow exact location, which apps use for maps, rides and delivery.

story.for_you: You see a prompt asking to use your location, with an option for precise. If you agree, the blue dot on the map shows your true spot, and maps, rides and delivery feel magical. You can switch it off any time.
story.for_makers: Makers need the exact spot for turn by turn directions, finding a driver and showing nearby places. It is also valuable to advertisers and data brokers. That is why platforms add prompts, reminders and the approximate option.

use_cases.example: A map app shows the blue dot on the right side of the street and reroutes you after a wrong turn.
A ride app finds the exact corner where the driver should pick you up.
An AR game places creatures at real places around you and needs your exact spot to match gyms and stops.
A food app shows the courier moving toward your door in real time.
A dating app shows how many meters away a match is.
A hidden kit records where you are many times a day and sells the trail to data brokers.

story.android_note: Android lets you grant fine or coarse location, with a one time and only while using option.
story.ios_note: iPhone has a Precise Location switch for each app and shows a blue arrow when location is in use.

technical_bounds: Needs location services on at the OS level
Background use needs a separate grant on both platforms
Status bar or Dynamic Island indicator while in use

abuse: Selling location trails to data brokers

linkedin.how: Privacy policy sections 1.5 and 2.1: LinkedIn asks members to opt in before using GPS or similar tools to identify precise location or proximity, used for tasks such as suggesting nearby members or calculating a commute. iOS label lists Precise Location (some purposes) as Linked to You.

history.change: Location became a runtime permission with an in-app prompt
Precise Location toggle added; apps can request one-time temporary full accuracy
Approximate option added; apps must request FINE together with COARSE
CLLocationUpdate async API and system-level location button in Share Location
